newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends off sharply after weak July expiry.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends off sharply after weak July expiry.

text.p: CME lumber futures closed sharply lower after a late fall sparked by a weak expiry to the July contract, floor sources said.
"When the July went off weak we just hit a bunch of sell stops (on September) and there was no buying at all," one floor trader said.
July fell $24.50 per thousand board feet to last trade at $350.00 per thousand board feet shortly after midday. It settled at $356.00, down $18.50.
Dealers said plentiful supplies in the cash market had led to little interest in taking delivery.
"There is plenty of wood available for prompt delivery at prices people are comfortable with," one dealer said.
September finished the $10.00 per tbf limit lower at $357.30. Dealers said the pool of unfilled sell orders was fairly small.
